faq.q: What is Andalusia Day and when is it in 2039?
faq.a: Andalusia Day (Día de Andalucía) is the region's official public holiday, celebrated annually on 28 February. In 2039 it falls on a Monday, making it perfect for a long weekend. It marks the 1980 referendum that granted Andalusia autonomy. Expect parades, flamenco, and free tapas across Marbella.

faq.q: Which yacht is best for a group celebration on Andalusia Day?
faq.a: For groups up to 12 guests, the Mangusta 80 (24m) offers ample deck space and a free jet ski – ideal for a party atmosphere. For smaller groups, the Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax) provides a flybridge lounge. All boats depart from Puerto Banús.

faq.q: What is included in the charter price?

faq.a: Yes, you are welcome to bring your own food, cakes, and decorations. Many guests bring Andalusian specialties like jamón, tortilla, and local wine. Just let us know in advance so we can prepare the boat accordingly. We also offer catering upgrades on request.

data.body_html:
Andalusia Day (28 February 2039) is the perfect excuse to gather friends and family for a memorable celebration on the water. With a yacht charter in Marbella, you can enjoy the region's famous coastline, sunshine, and festive atmosphere in style. Our fleet departs from Puerto Banús, offering options from €749 for two hours up to full-day charters with jet skis included. Whether you're marking the holiday with a group of 12 or an intimate party of 5, we have the right boat for you.

Why Celebrate Andalusia Day on a Yacht?

Andalusia Day is a public holiday across the region, with Marbella hosting parades, flamenco shows, and free tapas in the old town. But for a truly unique experience, nothing beats cruising the Mediterranean. You'll avoid the crowds, enjoy private service, and have the freedom to anchor at secluded coves like Cala Cortés or Cala del Faro. The weather in late February averages 18°C – perfect for sunbathing on deck.

What's Included in Your Charter

Every booking includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and 21% VAT. You can bring your own food and decorations – many guests bring Andalusian treats like jamón, olives, and local wine. For a premium experience, add a catering package or a DJ via our concierge service.

Sample Itinerary: 4-Hour Andalusia Day Cruise

  • 11:00 – Board at Puerto Banús, welcome drink of cava.
  • 11:15 – Depart east towards Cabopino. Spot the sand dunes of Artola.
  • 11:45 – Anchor at Cala del Faro for swimming and snacks.
  • 12:30 – Enjoy lunch on board (bring your own or order catering).
  • 13:30 – Cruise back, passing Marbella's Golden Mile and La Concha mountain.
  • 14:30 – Return to Puerto Banús.

Longer 8-hour charters can extend to Estepona or Sotogrande for lunch at a chiringuito.

Andalusia Day is a popular holiday, so we recommend booking early. Contact us via WhatsApp to check availability for your preferred boat and time. Our team will tailor the itinerary to your group's wishes. Visit our homepage to see the full fleet and start planning your celebration.
